description: The low-level building blocks of Wolfram Language graphics: 2D and 3D geometric primitives, color and style directives, lighting, and affine transformations. Everything drawn by the plotting functions is ultimately expressed in these terms, so they can be mixed freely with plots.

tools.name: Graphics
tools.description: Wraps a list of two-dimensional primitives and directives into a displayable graphic. Directives apply to all subsequent primitives in the same list, and nesting scopes them. It is the container every 2D plot ultimately returns.

parameters.name: PlotRange
parameters.description: Region of coordinate space to show.

parameters.name: AspectRatio
parameters.description: Automatic makes units equal in both directions.

tools.example:
Graphics[{EdgeForm[Black], LightBlue, Disk[{0, 0}, 1],
  Red, Thick, Line[{{-1, -1}, {1, 1}}]}, Axes -> True]

tools.name: Point
tools.description: Draws one point or a whole list of points at the given coordinates. A list argument is far more efficient than many separate Point primitives. Size is set with PointSize or AbsolutePointSize.
tools.notes: Point accepts VertexColors to color each point individually.

tools.name: Line
tools.description: Draws a polyline through a list of points, or several polylines when given a list of lists. Thickness, dashing and color come from the enclosing directives. It is the primitive behind every curve in a plot.

tools.name: Polygon
tools.description: Draws a filled polygon through the given vertices, in 2D or 3D. Holes can be specified by giving an inner boundary list. Polygon is also a valid geometric region for area and membership computations.
tools.example:
Graphics[{LightGreen, EdgeForm[Thick],
  Polygon[Table[{Cos[t], Sin[t]}, {t, 0, 2 Pi - 0.1, 2 Pi/7}]]}]
tools.notes: Area[Polygon[...]] and RegionMember[Polygon[...], pt] work directly on the same object.

tools.name: Circle
tools.description: Draws a circle, ellipse or circular arc outline. A two-element radius gives an ellipse, and a third argument restricts the angular range. Use Disk for the filled version.
tools.usage:
Circle[{x, y}, r]
Circle[{x, y}, {rx, ry}, {t1, t2}]
tools.example:
Graphics[{Circle[{0, 0}, 1], Red, Circle[{0, 0}, {1.5, 0.7}],
  Blue, Thick, Circle[{0, 0}, 2, {0, Pi/2}]}]

tools.name: Disk
tools.description: Draws a filled disk, ellipse or circular sector. Its argument forms mirror Circle, including an angular range for pie wedges. It is also a region object usable with Area and RegionMember.
tools.usage:
Disk[{x, y}, r]
Disk[{x, y}, r, {t1, t2}]

tools.name: Rectangle
tools.description: Draws a filled axis-aligned rectangle between two corner points. With one argument it draws a unit square at that corner. Use RoundingRadius for rounded corners.

tools.name: Arrow
tools.description: Draws an arrow along a line or curve, with heads whose size and shape are set by Arrowheads. A second argument sets back-off distances so the arrow does not touch the objects it connects. It works in both 2D and 3D.

tools.name: Arrowheads
tools.description: Directive that specifies the size, number, position and shape of arrowheads on subsequent Arrow primitives. Multiple heads can be placed along the shaft at given parameter positions. Custom graphics can be used as heads.

tools.name: Text
tools.description: Places a text or typeset expression at a given coordinate inside a graphic. Offset and direction arguments control alignment and rotation. Wrap the content in Style to set font size, weight and color.
tools.usage:
Text[expr, pos]
Text[expr, pos, offset, dir]
tools.notes: Inset places arbitrary graphics rather than text; Style controls appearance.

tools.name: BezierCurve
tools.description: Draws a composite Bezier curve through a list of control points, with the spline degree set by SplineDegree. Only the first and last control points are interpolated. Use it for smooth hand-shaped curves and arrow paths.

tools.name: BSplineCurve
tools.description: Draws a B-spline curve defined by control points, with options for degree, knots and closure. Compared with BezierCurve it offers local control, so moving one point affects only part of the curve. Use it for CAD-style smooth paths.

tools.name: BSplineSurface
tools.description: Draws a 3D B-spline surface from a grid of control points. It supports degree, knot and weight specification for full NURBS behaviour. Use it for freeform surface modelling inside Graphics3D.
tools.example:
pts = Table[{i, j, Sin[i] Cos[j]}, {i, 0, 3}, {j, 0, 3}];
Graphics3D[{BSplineSurface[pts]}, Boxed -> False]

tools.name: Sphere
tools.description: Draws a sphere of given center and radius in 3D, or a list of spheres in one primitive. It is also a geometric region, so Volume and RegionMember accept it. Use lists for efficient rendering of many particles.
tools.usage:
Sphere[{x, y, z}, r]
Sphere[{p1, p2, ...}, r]

tools.name: Cylinder
tools.description: Draws a filled cylinder between two endpoints with a given radius. It doubles as a solid region for measure and membership computations. Use it for rods, pipes and axis indicators in 3D scenes.
tools.usage: Cylinder[{{x1, y1, z1}, {x2, y2, z2}}, r]

tools.name: Cone
tools.description: Draws a cone with a circular base at the first point and apex at the second. Omitting the radius gives a default unit cone. It is useful for arrowheads, nozzles and direction markers in 3D.

tools.name: Cuboid
tools.description: Draws an axis-aligned box between two opposite corners, or a unit cube from one corner. Lists of cuboids render efficiently for voxel-style scenes. As a region it supports Volume and RegionMember.
tools.usage:
Cuboid[{xmin, ymin, zmin}, {xmax, ymax, zmax}]
Cuboid[{x, y, z}]

tools.name: Tube
tools.description: Draws a tube of given radius around a 3D curve or line, giving curves visible thickness. Radii may vary along the curve when given as a list. Use it for space curves, field lines and molecular bonds.
tools.example:
ParametricPlot3D[{Cos[t], Sin[t], t/5}, {t, 0, 6 Pi},
  PlotStyle -> Tube[0.15], Boxed -> False]

tools.name: Raster
tools.description: Draws an array of values or colors as a grid of rectangular cells inside a graphic. It is the primitive behind image display and array plots. Use it to place pixel data at precise coordinates in a scene.
tools.notes: Raster3D is the voxel analogue; ArrayPlot is a higher-level wrapper with legends and labels.

tools.name: RGBColor
tools.description: Specifies a color by red, green and blue components in the range 0 to 1, with an optional alpha. It is the most direct way to set an exact color. Hexadecimal strings such as "#3366cc" are also accepted.
tools.usage:
RGBColor[r, g, b]
RGBColor[r, g, b, a]
RGBColor["#rrggbb"]

tools.name: Hue
tools.description: Specifies a color by hue, with optional saturation, brightness and opacity. Cycling hue from 0 to 1 sweeps the color wheel, which makes it convenient for generating distinguishable series colors. Values outside 0 to 1 wrap around.

tools.name: GrayLevel
tools.description: Specifies a shade of gray from 0 (black) to 1 (white), with an optional opacity. It is the standard directive for monochrome figures and subtle grid styling. Many built-in styles use it internally.
tools.example:
Plot[Sin[x], {x, 0, 2 Pi}, GridLinesStyle -> GrayLevel[0.85],
  GridLines -> Automatic]

tools.name: Opacity
tools.description: Directive that sets the transparency of subsequent objects, where 0 is fully transparent and 1 fully opaque. It can also wrap a color to produce a translucent version of it. Essential for layered 2D plots and for seeing inside 3D scenes.
tools.example:
Graphics3D[{Opacity[0.35, Red], Sphere[{0, 0, 0}, 1],
  Opacity[0.35, Blue], Sphere[{0.8, 0, 0}, 1]}]

tools.name: Thickness
tools.description: Sets line width as a fraction of the overall graphic width, so lines scale with the figure. Use AbsoluteThickness for widths in printer's points that do not scale. The named directives Thin and Thick are convenient shorthands.

tools.name: Dashing
tools.description: Directive that draws subsequent lines as dashes with the given segment lengths, expressed as fractions of the graphic width. An offset argument shifts the dash pattern. Dashed, Dotted and DotDashed are preset shorthands.

tools.name: PointSize
tools.description: Sets the diameter of drawn points as a fraction of the graphic width. AbsolutePointSize gives a fixed size in points instead. Named sizes Tiny, Small, Medium and Large are accepted.

tools.name: EdgeForm
tools.description: Directive specifying how the edges of filled 2D and 3D shapes are drawn. Give None for edgeless fills or a Directive for colored, thick or dashed outlines. It pairs naturally with FaceForm.

tools.name: FaceForm
tools.description: Directive specifying how the faces of filled shapes are rendered, including separate front and back appearance in 3D. Use FaceForm[None] to draw only edges. It complements EdgeForm.

tools.name: Lighting
tools.description: Option controlling the light sources in a 3D scene, accepting named schemes such as "Neutral" and "Accent" or an explicit list of ambient, directional, point and spot lights. Lighting strongly affects how surface shape is perceived. Use "Neutral" when true surface colors matter.

tools.name: Specularity
tools.description: Directive that gives subsequent 3D surfaces a specular highlight, with an intensity and an exponent controlling tightness. Higher exponents produce smaller, sharper highlights typical of polished materials. Combine with Glow and surface color for material effects.

tools.name: Rotate
tools.description: Rotates a graphics object or expression by a given angle about a point or axis. In 2D it takes an angle and optional center; in 3D an axis is also given. It works on text and whole graphics, not just primitives.
tools.usage:
Rotate[expr, theta]
Rotate[expr, theta, {x, y}]
Rotate[expr, theta, axis, center]

tools.name: Translate
tools.description: Shifts a graphics object by a vector, or replicates it at several offsets when given a list of vectors. It is the cheapest way to tile a motif across a scene. Works identically in 2D and 3D.

tools.name: Scale
tools.description: Scales a graphics object by a uniform or per-axis factor about a given center. Negative factors produce reflections. Use it to stretch motifs without recomputing their coordinates.

tools.name: GeometricTransformation
tools.description: Applies an arbitrary transformation, given as a TransformationFunction, matrix or {matrix, vector} pair, to graphics primitives. A list of transformations replicates the object once per transformation. It is the general mechanism behind Rotate, Translate and Scale.
tools.notes: Transformation constructors include RotationTransform, TranslationTransform, ScalingTransform, ReflectionTransform, ShearingTransform and AffineTransform.

tools.name: RotationTransform
tools.description: Builds a TransformationFunction representing a rotation by an angle, optionally about a specified center or 3D axis. The result can be applied to points directly or used inside GeometricTransformation. Use it whenever you need the transformation as a reusable object.
tools.usage:
RotationTransform[theta]
RotationTransform[theta, {x, y}]
RotationTransform[theta, axis, center]

tools.name: ColorData
tools.description: Gives access to named color gradients and color schemes, either as a single color from a gradient or as the whole scheme. ColorData["Gradients"] lists all continuous gradients and ColorData[n] gives indexed default plot colors. It is the standard source of consistent colors in visualizations.
tools.notes: ColorData[97] is the default line-plot color scheme; ColorData["scheme", "Panel"] previews a scheme.

tools.name: Blend
tools.description: Interpolates between two or more colors, returning the color at a given fraction. Given a list of {position, color} pairs it builds a custom gradient. Use it to create tailored color functions for plots.

tools.name: Lighter
tools.description: Returns a lighter version of a color, by default blending it halfway toward white. A second argument gives the blending fraction. Use it together with Darker to build tonal variations of a base palette.

tools.name: Darker
tools.description: Returns a darker version of a color by blending it toward black. The optional fraction controls how far. It is the counterpart of Lighter and is widely used for edge and text colors.
